title: Guide exercise: diagnosis, blocking
description: A starter on a fresh problem: the loop of the library example diagnosis with every refinement replaced by a block. Find the interface, write a refinement, and compare with diagnosis. See the guide page "Checks that look for a witness, and cores".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% A full adder: gate(Name, Kind, Input1, Input2, Output).
gate(x1,xor,a,b,p).
gate(x2,xor,p,c,s).
gate(a1,and,a,b,q).
gate(a2,and,p,c,r).
gate(o1,or,q,r,co).
wire(a;b;c;p;q;r;s;co).
% Observed: with inputs a = 1, b = 0, c = 1 the adder shows sum s = 1 and carry co = 0
% (it should show s = 0 and co = 1).
obs(a,1). obs(b,0). obs(c,1). obs(s,1). obs(co,0).
% Is gate x2 part of a minimal diagnosis?
% gate(Name, Kind, Input1, Input2, Output), wire(X), obs(X,Value); the constant
% suspect names a gate.
part(G) :- gate(G,_,_,_,_).
fragments.description: Derived facts about the circuit. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: circuit
fragments.text:
% How the circuit behaves in a world W. Solver A uses the world "now" (the candidate),
% solver C the world "alt" (the counterexample); the rules are written once.
% on(W,X): wire X carries 1 in world W.  broken(W,G): gate G is assumed faulty there.
out(W,G) :- gate(G,and,X,Y,_), on(W,X), on(W,Y).
out(W,G) :- gate(G,or,X,_,_), on(W,X).
out(W,G) :- gate(G,or,_,Y,_), on(W,Y).
out(W,G) :- gate(G,xor,X,Y,_), on(W,X), not on(W,Y).
out(W,G) :- gate(G,xor,X,Y,_), on(W,Y), not on(W,X).
% A gate that is not broken computes its function; a broken gate may output anything.
:- world(W), gate(G,_,_,_,Z), not broken(W,G), on(W,Z), not out(W,G).
:- world(W), gate(G,_,_,_,Z), not broken(W,G), not on(W,Z), out(W,G).
% The observations hold.
:- world(W), obs(X,1), not on(W,X).
:- world(W), obs(X,0), on(W,X).
fragments.description: The behaviour of the circuit in a world; used by solver A and by solver C.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a set of broken gates and a value for every wire that fit the
% observations (the circuit fragment sees to that for the world "now").
world(now).
{ broken(now,G) } :- part(G).
{ on(now,X) } :- wire(X).
% Is the suspect gate part of a minimal diagnosis? (Each instance sets the constant.)
:- not broken(now,suspect).
#show.
#show broken(G) : broken(now,G).
#show on(X) : on(now,X).
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): broken gates and wire values that fit the observations.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: which gates the candidate breaks. The wire values stay private to solver A.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: the observations can also be explained in a world "alt" in which a
% proper subset of the candidate's gates is broken. The wires may take other values.
world(alt).
{ broken(alt,G) } :- broken(now,G).
{ on(alt,X) } :- wire(X).
mended(G) :- broken(now,G), not broken(alt,G).
fewer :- mended(G).
:- not fewer.
#show.
#show broken(G) : broken(alt,G).

% The smaller explanation refutes every candidate that breaks its gates and at least
% one more. Mark its gates and, as a witness, the first gate it mends.
relevant(broken(now,G)) :- broken(alt,G).
relevant(broken(now,G)) :- mended(G), not mended(H) : part(H), H < G.
fragments.description: Looks for an explanation that breaks fewer gates (solver C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + circuit + abstraction
solver C = shared + circuit + check     options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)
